metadata.creator: Upham, Alfred H.
metadata.description: Alfred H. Upham, president of Miami University, writes to Mr. Koichi Hasegawa in Osaka, Japan, regarding the Upham family's planned winter trip to Japan. He provides their expected itinerary, including arrivals in Yokohama and Kioto, hotel reservations in Tokyo and Kioto, and a planned departure from Kobe, and states that Hasegawa should not feel obligated to show them around.
metadata.title: Letter to Mr. Koichi Hasegawa from the president, 19 October 1937
metadata.transcript:
[page 1]
October 19, 1937

Mr. [Mister] Koichi Hasegawa
57 Naka 1 Chome [Naka first district]
Sonezaki, Kitaku [Kita Ward]
Osaka, Japan

My dear Hasegawa:

In spite of many discouragements the Upham family is still planning quite definitely a winter vacation which will take the form of a trip around the world. We shall have to be detoured around China, but, we still have every assurance that your country will be open to visitors and that we shall have every opportunity to get around. I have heard from Dr. [Doctor] Shideler, who has been in Japan until very recently and who I believe saw you during his visit there. We would be glad also to see you sometime and some place which proves to be convenient for you during our all too limited stay in the country.

Our present plan is to reach Yokohama on the President Hoover on the morning of Saturday, November 27. We have reservations at the Imperial Hotel in Tokyo for several days. We are to reach Kioto [Kyoto] Wednesday afternoon, December 1, and will be at the Miyako Hotel there. We plan to sail from Kobe Sunday, December 5. I am writing you these details so that it may be easier for you to establish contact with us, and not with the thought that you should feel any obligation what-ever to show us around or do things for us. We have arranged a rather busy itinerary with the American Express, and hope that the rather unusual conditions now prevailing will not interfere too seriously with what we should like to see.

With all good wishes,

Very truly yours,

President
